primitives.name: Closing Line Value Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: GSE's public standard is *closing-line value*, not "we found +EV at open." Also: pick lifecycle should timestamp the line at **lock** and compare **NEXTWAVE-YES** - `2008.01485` — Wisdom of crowds: much ado about nothing — **[C2][C4]**.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'CLV': 'dimensionless score bounded [0,1], normalized against Brier loss', 't_lock': 'timestamp of event lock in UTC seconds', 't_close': 'timestamp of final line closure in UTC seconds'}

primitives.breakdown_regime: When t_close < t_lock or line drift exceeds 10% of initial spread.

primitives.name: Brier-CLV Diagnostic Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Code focus - `line-archive` - `money observability` - `performance CLV diagnostics` ## Done when CLV↔Brier diagnostic when archive exists; lock≠open doctrine in docs; no ROI claims in public copy.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B_score': 'Brier score, dimensionless, lower is better', 'CLV': 'Closing Line Value, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Archived line data is complete and consistent; CLV and Brier are jointly informative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B_score > 0.25 or CLV < 0.45 across 100+ samples.

primitives.verbatim_quote: - `1211.6496` (score 13) TwitterPaul: Extracting and Aggregating Twitter Predictions — Build a 'crowd wisdom' auxiliary signal from social media predictions as one member of GSE's multiplicative-weight ensemble (CEPT), weighted dynamically based on historical forecaster accuracy.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{S}_{\\text{social}}(t)': 'Social ensemble signal at time t, dimensionless', 'w_i(t)': 'Dynamic weight of forecaster i at time t, [0,1]', 'p_i^{\\text{tweet}}(t)': 'Predictive probability from forecaster i at time t, [0,1]'}
primitives.assumptions: Twitter predictions are independent and informative; weights update via historical MAE.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ensemble variance exceeds 0.15 or individual weight drops below 0.05.

layer2.telemetry: Ensemble entropy and dynamic weight stability metrics.
